title: The Last Safehouse Revisited
premise: Cyrus Underhill, a hostage negotiator who walked away from the agency that trained him after a botched extraction left one hostage dead, learns the remote safe house where he hid for years has been listed online — interior photos and all. The listing is bait: his old handlers are flushing out every operative who ever passed through their off-books network. To survive, Cyrus must go on offense, dismantling the program from within while dodging the very people who taught him to disappear. In the end he trades himself to save the last innocent caught in the network's web, burning the safe house — and his own anonymity — as the price of finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: Petra Coldharbour is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people talk their way back from the edge. She writes thrillers about the conversations that decide who lives.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Insomniac Cyrus scrolls real estate sites at 3 a.m. and finds the safe house for sale — with photos of his own handwriting on the kitchen wall. He recognizes the staging as tradecraft, not commerce. Emotional beat: cold dread; the past has found an address.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Flashback braided with present: how he fled after the Marlowe extraction failure, what the network promised in exchange for silence. He packs a go-bag he never unpacked. Beat: grief resurfacing under routine.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Agent
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A cheerful agent named Delia Voss shows up at his current flat claiming to represent the seller — and knows details no stranger should. Cyrus plays dumb, feeds her false timelines. Beat: the hunter wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Marlowe, Again
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. He visits the widow of the hostage who died, seeking the file he never read. She gives him a box of evidence she's kept out of spite. Beat: guilt made physical; a door he swore stayed shut opens.

chapters.title: The Program Called Lantern
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Decoding the widow's documents, he maps Lantern: a deniable training pipeline for negotiators used as disposable assets. His name appears three times. Beat: horror of seeing yourself as inventory.

chapters.title: Delia's Other Client
chapters.summary: POV Delia Voss. Reveal chapter: Delia is a former Lantern asset turned fixer, hired to confirm which safe houses are still 'occupied.' She suspects Cyrus is more than a witness. Beat: mirrored loneliness, two survivors circling.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Someone torches his car with a warning note inside: COME HOME OR WE SELL THE REST. He realizes other safe houses are being listed too — live operatives exposed one by one. Beat: urgency ignites; the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Man Who Trained Me
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. He tracks down Aldous Renner, his old instructor, now retired and terrified. Renner admits Lantern is being liquidated by its own founders to erase liability. Beat: betrayal by the father figure; reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Safe House Seven
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Delia reaches Safe House Seven first and finds a young asset, Noor, hiding there — the last trainee still in the dark. Instead of reporting her, Delia hesitates. Beat: conscience cracking the professional shell.

chapters.title: Three-Way Call
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus negotiates remotely between Noor, panicking in the safe house, and the cleanup team approaching outside — his old skills weaponized for someone else's survival. Beat: redemption rehearsal; he talks a life off the ledge.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The widow reveals her husband was Lantern's accountant; the box contains ledger pages naming the founders. One founder is now a government liaison. Beat: scale widens from personal to institutional.

chapters.title: Renner's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Dying of illness, Renner records testimony but insists Cyrus use it as leverage, not justice. Their argument over means vs. ends turns bitter. Beat: mentor and student at ideological knifepoint.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The founders list the final safe house — Cyrus's original one — with an open-house date. It's an invitation. He decides to attend, armed with the ledger. Beat: dread and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Delia's Price
chapters.summary: POV Delia. The handlers confront Delia about Noor's escape; she kills her handler's trust instead of Noor, going rogue. She brings Cyrus the floor plans. Beat: defection; belonging chosen over survival.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus walks into the staged safe house among real buyers, reading the room like a negotiation — identifying the founders' security chief by his breathing patterns. Beat: taut suspense; the prey tours the trap.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Wall
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Alone upstairs, Cyrus finds his own message preserved behind fresh paint: names of everyone Lantern burned. The founders kept it as insurance against each other. Beat: eerie intimacy with his past self.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus confronts the surviving founder, offering the ledger and Renner's recording in exchange for Noor's clean exit. The founder counters: Cyrus himself, delivered quietly. Beat: the negotiation of his life — with his own life as the subject.

chapters.title: Renner's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Renner releases the recording publicly before dying, forcing the founders' hand and destroying Cyrus's leverage — deliberately, so Cyrus can't sell himself. Beat: furious gratitude; the final lesson is that some prices shouldn't be paid.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. With the network collapsing, the security chief comes for the wall of names. Cyrus and Delia burn the safe house themselves, denying the founders their insurance and erasing the last proof of who Cyrus was. Beat: cathartic destruction; identity surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unlisted
chapters.summary: POV Delia. Delia gets Noor across the border and declines a new identity offer, choosing to stay findable. She writes Cyrus one line: the house sold. Beat: quiet hope; belonging without hiding.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus testifies under a deal that exposes him fully — name, history, failure — and walks out into daylight with nothing hidden. That night he sleeps through till morning for the first time since Marlowe. Beat: release; survival's price paid in visibility.

chapters.title: The Last Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, coda. Months later, Cyrus teaches negotiation to civilians, keeps the widow's box on his shelf, and lets Delia and Noor into his small life. The final safe house, he realizes, was never a building. Beat: belonging earned; the story closes on an open door.
